proposal: The Mandate recommends that the administration follow the language of Executive Order 13834 (agencies prioritize reducing waste, cutting costs, improving resilience and mission accomplishment) and direct the Federal Energy Management Program to help agencies follow the law and use energy efficiently and cost-effectively rather than meeting aggressive extra-statutory renewable-energy goals, with a much smaller budget.
remaining: An order or guidance restating Executive Order 13834 principles for agency operations (page 386; none found)
A FEMP program reorientation to cost-effective statutory goals and a reduced budget (page 386; not found)
Final repeal of the fossil-fuel restrictions rule (stay only so far)

flags: Progress lowered from 40 to 30 within in_progress because only the removal of the extra-statutory goals and a compliance stay are operative; neither the positive Executive Order 13834 direction nor any FEMP refocus or budget cut was found.
review.mandate_note: Pages 385 to 386 ask the administration to follow Executive Order 13834's direction that agencies reduce waste, cut costs, improve resilience and support their missions, and to focus FEMP on helping agencies meet statutory energy goals efficiently and cost-effectively with much less money, rather than extra-statutory renewable goals.

source_checks.note: Notification of stay published 2026-09-02 moves the compliance date from 2026-09-01 to 2027-03-01; no repeal proposed (checked 2026-10-15).

significance.rationale: Redirecting federal agency energy management away from renewable goals affects federal operations government-wide but costs and savings are small.

status_summary: Executive Order 14148, signed 2025-01-20, revoked in section 2(rr) Executive Order 14057 on federal sustainability, the order that had replaced Executive Order 13834. On 2025-05-05 DOE stayed the compliance date of its rule on clean energy for new federal buildings and major renovations while it reviewed its guidance, and on 2026-09-02 it further stayed that compliance date from 2026-09-01 to 2027-03-01 while it reviews the 2024 rule. No replacement order restating Executive Order 13834 principles and no change to FEMP's own program or budget was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14148 was signed and, in section 2(rr), revoked Executive Order 14057 of 2021 on federal sustainability.

DOE published a stay of the compliance date for its rule on clean energy for new federal buildings and major renovations (10 CFR parts 433 and 435), pending review of guidance for alignment with current energy policies; stay to 2026-05-01.
DOE published a notification further staying the compliance date of the 10 CFR parts 433 and 435 requirements from 2026-09-01 to 2027-03-01 while it reviews the 2024 final rule.

title: Refocus federal energy management on cost-effective use, not climate targets
uncertainties: The 2026 notice carries a title referring to repeal but only extends a stay; the move of the compliance date from 2026-09-01 implies an intermediate stay not separately recorded here. Whether a replacement federal operations order exists, and any FEMP staffing or program change, were not found; the FY2027 budget summary page read did not mention FEMP and FY2026 and FY2027 FEMP requests were not located. Searches run on federalregister.gov, fedcenter.gov and budget summaries.
